deep.reconstruction:
Setting (genus 3, plane quartic; the equations (6), (7) are on an earlier page and are inferred here). The quartic is F=0 with (6) F = f^2 - x y z t, where x, y, z, t are linear forms that vanish on bitangents and f is a conic. The 'Abelian functions' √x, √y, ... are the square roots of the 28 bitangent forms; they are single-valued on the curve up to factors ±1 across the cuts (Querschnitte). From what the page uses, the second equation of (7) must be pq = zt + 2αf + α²xy [my inference]. Here α is a parameter chosen so that the right-hand side splits into two linear factors p, q.

Step 1. Multiply by zt and use xyzt = f² from (6):
pqzt = z²t² + 2αf·zt + α²xyzt = z²t² + 2αfzt + α²f² = (zt + αf)².
Hence [my step]
(zt + αf)² - pqzt = α²(f² - xyzt) = α²F.
So F = 0 can be rewritten as f'² - pqzt = 0 with the conic f' = (zt + αf)/α. That is, the pair (p,q) together with (z,t) gives the same normal form as (x,y),(z,t).

Step 2. Starting from the pair √x, √y one obtains 6 pairs: √(xy), √(zt), √(p_i q_i) for i=1..4. Any two of them bring F into the form f² - xyzt = 0.
- [My remark] The splitting condition is that the 3×3 determinant of zt + 2αf + α²xy vanishes. This is a sextic in α whose roots include α=0 and α=∞, leaving 4 further pairs.

Step 3. Monodromy argument. A product of two of these square roots is rational on the curve. So all six products must acquire the same factors (±1) across the cuts. These factor systems are determined by the sum mod 2 of the two characteristics. Therefore all 6 pairs of a 'Gruppe' have the same characteristic sum, called the 'Gruppencharakteristik'.

Step 4. On the curve f = √(xy)√(zt) (with a suitable sign). From (7):
2f = (pq - zt)/α - αxy = 2√(xy)√(zt),
so pq = α²xy + 2α√(xy)√(zt) + zt = (√(zt) + α√(xy))².
This gives (8): √(pq) = √(zt) + α√(xy).
Thus every product in a group is a linear combination of any two products of the same group.

Step 5. Counting. The 28 odd theta functions give 28·27/2 = 378 = 6·63 pairs. These fall into 63 groups of 6 pairs, one for each nonzero characteristic. To obtain the group of a characteristic g, write g in the 6 possible ways as a sum of two odd characteristics.

Example: g = (001/000). The parity is q(c) = Σ ε_i ε_i'. Adding g flips ε_3, which changes the parity by ε_3'. So the relevant odd c are exactly those with ε_3' = 0 whose genus-2 part is one of the 6 odd genus-2 characteristics:
(10/10), (01/01), (11/10), (11/01), (10/11), (01/11).
Each such part, with ε_3 = 0 and with ε_3 = 1, gives one pair. These are the six pairs listed.

Step 6. Final claim, without proof on the page: if three pairs of a group are known, the remaining pairs are obtained by solving a cubic equation.
errors: No mathematical error found. All six listed decompositions of (001/000) are pairs of odd characteristics summing to (001/000), and 378 = 6·63.
Implicit, not an error: the identity f = √(xy)√(zt) requires a choice of sign of the square roots on the curve. Formula (8) likewise holds only with a coherent sign convention, which is not stated.
Implicit: the claim that there are exactly 4 further pairs p_i q_i besides xy and zt (from the sextic-in-α splitting condition) is asserted without argument on this page.
Implicit: the closing claim about the cubic equation is stated without proof on this page.

results.what: Rewriting the quartic f²=xyzt as f'²=pqzt via pq = zt+2αf+α²xy, giving 6 pairs of bitangents per such family
results.modern_name: Steiner complexes / syzygetic representation of a plane quartic as a sum of products of bitangents (quadratic determinantal / Steiner groups)
results.usually_credited_to: Steiner (1855), Hesse (1855); in theta-function form Riemann (lectures 1861/62, publ. Werke 1876) and H. Weber (1876)

results.what: Products of pairs in a group have the same factor system, so pairs in a group share the same characteristic sum (group characteristic)
results.modern_name: Steiner complex associated to a nonzero 2-torsion point / characteristic; sum of two odd theta characteristics
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann ('Zur Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen für den Fall p=3', Werke 1876), Weber 1876

results.what: √(pq) = √(zt) + α√(xy): linear relation among the square roots of products within a group
results.modern_name: Riemann's linear relations among square roots of bitangent products; normal form √(xξ)+√(yη)+√(zζ)=0

results.what: 378 pairs = 63 groups × 6 pairs; each nonzero characteristic is a sum of two odd characteristics in exactly 6 ways
results.modern_name: 63 Steiner complexes of the 28 bitangents / 2-torsion of Jacobian of genus 3 curve

results.what: Given three pairs of a group, the other three come from a cubic equation
results.modern_name: Determination of a Steiner complex from partial data

deep.surprise_reason: This is the standard content of Riemann's 1861/62 lectures on p=3, published posthumously as 'Zur Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen für den Fall p=3' in the Werke (1876), and expanded by Weber in the same year. The 63 groups of 6 pairs are Steiner's (1855). Nothing here goes beyond what is already attributed to Riemann. The handwriting may be a copyist's or auditor's Nachschrift rather than Riemann's autograph.

transcription_corrections: The hand appears to be a fair-copy/Nachschrift hand rather than Riemann's autograph; worth flagging for attribution.
'Greifen wir demnach von zwei beliebigen...' is more likely 'Gehen wir demnach von zwei beliebigen Abel'schen Functionen √x, √y aus'.
'Jede der von (000/000) verschiedenen 63 Charakteristiken ist eine Gruppencharakteristik' is more likely than 'ist kann'. The image suggests 'ist eine'.
The group characteristic in the example is (001/000), i.e. top row 001 and bottom row 000. The listed pairs, with ε3 toggled and bottom ε3'=0, are confirmed consistent by checking parity and sums.
'Ueberschreiten der Querschnitte' is plausible; the struck-through words after 'Querschnitten' are illegible deletions.
In the line 'Aus den Gleichungen (7.) und (6.)', the insertion '(6.)' is written above the line, consistent with the use of f = √(xy)√(zt).
